title: Agent Lifecycle: Plan → Act → Evaluate
summary: Structure agent systems, integrate them into the SDLC, define the planning/execution boundary, configure observability, and right-size human oversight.

blocks.body: The agent lifecycle is the foundational model for all agentic AI in GitHub. Every agent task follows three distinct, ordered phases — they must not be collapsed.

blocks.text: **📋 Plan:** The agent receives inputs and produces a _structured plan artifact_ — a file, PR comment, or structured workflow output that describes what it intends to do. This artifact is inspectable and validatable before any action occurs.
**⚡ Act:** Only after the plan is approved (by a human gate or automated status check) does the agent execute. Actions: write code, commit to branch, create PR, call external APIs via MCP.
**📊 Evaluate:** Automated scanning tools and human reviewers assess outputs against predefined success criteria. Results feed back into the next iteration.

items: Agents differ from assistants: they _act_ on the codebase autonomously, not just suggest
Planning and execution must be **distinct, separated steps** — never combined
The plan artifact is the contract between the agent and the reviewer
Evaluation signals: quantitative (test pass rate) AND qualitative (code readability)

blocks.text: **Exam Tip:** Combining plan and act in one step is the #1 documented anti-pattern. If asked which comes first — always Plan, then validate, then Act.
